# Intent - phase-bj: mechanical close flow

Written 2026-10-18 by fenix from Rand's rulings of 2026-10-18 (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, docs PR atm-bd-orchestration #342). One page at most. Jev questions are judged against the anchors, not this document.

## What this plan is for

Dev work is not complete until sanity verifies it, and nothing between a dev
push and the QA assignment should need the lead. Today the dev closes its own
task on push, the lead hand-assigns every sanity and QA task, and atm-bd has
never issued an assignment because its dispatch reads branch and worktree
from beads the pour never wrote them to. This phase makes the dev, fix,
sanity and qa closes one script, `atm-task-close.py`, that verifies the
minimum (PR open on `pr_target`, pushed head, rebased), closes the bead,
reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead; the dev's
task stays open until sanity passes.

## What success looks like

- A dev or fix bead closes only through the hook; the dev's ATM task is closed by the sanity hook on PASS and the dev waits meanwhile.
- Sanity and QA assignment never need the lead: the hook assigns, atm-bd assigns a ready bead with no task, both as the phase lead.
- A sanity FAIL reopens the bead and sends the dev `sanity-rejected` on the same task and branch; `max_sanity_rounds` (default 5) escalates to the lead.
- The pour writes branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty to every bead of a sprint family and a pydantic model per bead kind validates the whole phase.
- atm-core issue #1873 (task transition hooks, 1.6.2) is the long-term home; the skill script stands in until it ships.
- Sanity links the layer on PASS under the stack bead's claim: the stack bead holds the whole stack as ledger and lock, first PASS wins the top and the loser gets `rebase-required` (no round counted); a sanity-stack subagent handles one next-top layer per spawn, sequentially, with a lean mode and a lock timeout that never blocks the team.

## What is deliberately out of scope

- Mechanical dev or fix assignment: the lead picks the dev (ANC-060).
- Whole-stack verification in the hook: the lead owns stack hygiene (ANC-054, ANC-062).
- The small phase-bi console fixes (self-addressed send, icons, agent rows): they close in phase-bi.

## Anchors

The phase-bi anchors (ANC-001..050, REQ-BI6-AC6) are carried unchanged in
`anchors.json` so Jev judges phase-bj items against the same console
rulings; ANC-051..086 are this phase's; ANC-063 and ANC-074 are retired and replaced by ANC-078..083 and ANC-084..086, respectively (ANC-062 retired to ANC-065). Rendered to `anchors.md`.

item.text:
# phase-bj: mechanical close flow: close hook, stack bead, sanity-stack, runs tabs

## Description

Repository: randlee/atm-bd-orchestration. Code, worktrees, sprint branches and PRs live there, on its `integrate/phase-bj`; atm-core's `integrate/phase-bj` holds only this plan. The rulings are Rand's of 2026-10-18, anchored as ANC-051..088 in `docs/plans/phase-bj/anchors.md` (ANC-062 retired by ANC-065); the requirement docs are `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` and `docs/requirements/sanity-stack.md` of atm-bd-orchestration PR #342 with the dev, dev-sanity, team-lead and quality-mgr requirement items they amend.

### Goal
Dev work is not complete until sanity verifies it, and the lead does not need to intervene between a dev push and the QA assignment:
- one script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes; it checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead (ANC-051..059, ANC-070);
- the dev's ATM task stays open until the sanity close hook closes it on PASS; a sanity FAIL is one `sanity-fail.xml.j2` message to the dev on that open task, no finding children, counted in `metadata.sanity_round` up to `max_sanity_rounds` (default 5) (ANC-055..057, ANC-072);
- the stack bead `<prefix>-phase-<x>.stack` is the ledger and the lock of the phase stack; the sanity side links the layer on PASS under its claim, first PASS wins the top and the other dev gets `rebase-required` without a round counted; a sanity-stack subagent handles one next-top layer per spawn, sequentially, with a lean mode and a lock timeout that never blocks the team and never escalates to a person (ANC-065..069, ANC-071);
- the pour writes branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty onto every generated dev, fix, sanity and QA bead and validates the projected phase graph before writes (ANC-083, atm-bd-orchestration #340);
- `atm-bd console` shows a sanity runs tab and a quality runs tab, newest first, QA run-level verdict and elapsed, the dev's name and icon, and an API_FAILURE kind distinct from a FAIL verdict (ANC-073, atm-bd-orchestration #347).

Dev and fix assignment stay the lead's (ANC-060); atm-bd assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task (ANC-061).

No per-reviewer quality metadata is promised: the producer is outside phase-bj, so the quality tab displays only fields and findings already written by in-scope producers.

### Sprints
| Sprint | Title | Relation | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| bj-1 | close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds | root | - |
| bj-2 | stack bead and sprint-family pour: stack-bead.json.j2, pour metadata, pydantic model per bead kind, validate-plan | root | - |
| bj-3 | sanity-stack subagent and dev-sanity PASS wiring: sequential spawns, lock timeout, lean mode | must_follow | bj-1, bj-2 |
| bj-4 | console sanity and quality runs tabs; measured elapsed and dev identity in the sanity ledger | parallel_safe | - |
| bj-5 | out-of-band full-skill integrity manifest; install verification and hand-runnable plugin doctor | parallel_safe | - |

`requirements` and `adrs` are `NONE` on every sprint: the atm-core requirement and ADR documents do not govern atm-bd-orchestration code; the governing text is the package's `docs/requirements/*.md` named per sprint.

### BJ5 integrity addition (atm-bd-orchestration #349)
`bj-5` publishes an out-of-band sc-sha manifest for all shipped skill files, verifies files against the selected release manifest during `atm-bd skill` install, and ships a hand-runnable plugin doctor reporting per-file status and aggregate PASS/FAIL. It uses sc-compose's Python sc-sha implementation, stores no SHA inside any file, leaves sc-publish unchanged, and has no dependency on atm-core. Anchors: ANC-087, ANC-088. requirements/adrs: NONE.

## Acceptance criteria

### Success Criteria
- A dev bead closed through `atm-task-close.py --role dev` in a scratch repository leaves the dev's ATM task open, closes the bead, and assigns the sanity task as the phase lead with no lead action (ANC-052, ANC-055).
- A sanity PASS through the hook closes the dev's task as the lead and assigns QA as the lead; a sanity FAIL sends one `sanity-fail` message on the dev's open task and creates no bead (ANC-053, ANC-056, ANC-072).
- Two branches cut from the same top that both pass sanity: the first advances the stack bead from empty to singleton against trunk, the second is linked as the hosted top in `layers`; a conflicting second branch gets `rebase-required` and `sanity_round` does not move (ANC-065, ANC-067, ANC-071).
- `validate-plan --phase bj` requires the stack bead and every generated dev, fix, sanity and QA bead carries branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty (ANC-083).
- `atm-bd console` shows the sanity and quality tabs with run-level QA verdict and elapsed, the dev's icon and name, and an API_FAILURE icon distinct from FAIL (ANC-073).
- Every sprint's QA PASS at its head; the stack lands on `integrate/phase-bj` of atm-bd-orchestration; `just lint` and `just test` green there.
- `atm-bd skill` verifies every installed file against the selected release manifest and refuses mismatches with the path list; `atm-hook-doctor.py` reports per-file integrity and aggregate PASS/FAIL from the install-recorded manifest, using sc-compose's Python sc-sha implementation only (ANC-087, ANC-088).
- Phase BJ5 uses no atm-core dependency, embeds no SHA in shipped files, and leaves sc-publish unchanged.
